sources.title: The Bund Shanghai Travel Guide (2026): Sights, Dining & Tips
sources.content:
The Bund, nestled along the Huangpu River in Shanghai's Huangpu District, is a renowned historical and cultural street stretching 1.5 kilometers from Yan'an East Road to Waibaidu Bridge. Features 52 classical revival buildings representing the World Architecture Exhibition.

Hours: Open 24/7. Lighting: 7-11 PM (summer), 6-10 PM (winter). Best Visit: Sunset through evening. Duration: 1-2 hours leisurely, half-day for deep exploration.

Main Attractions: Huangpu Park (People's Heroes Monument), Waibaidu Bridge (52.16-meter dual spans), Shiliupu Dock (730-meter waterside platform, 270-degree views), Chen Yi Square (5.6-meter bronze statue), Lovers' Wall (1,700-meter decorative flood wall), Bund Sightseeing Tunnel (646.7m, 50 RMB), Origin of the Bund (Waitanyuan).

Notable Buildings: BUND 22, Asia Building, Waldorf Astoria Hotel, HSBC Building, Peace Hotel, Bank of China Building.

River Cruises: Budget Ferry 2 RMB (10-minute journey). Sightseeing Cruise 120-150 RMB (2-3 hours).

Dining: ROOF P.M. Modern Dining (19.9 RMB minimum), POP Rooftop Dining, Kathleen's Waitan K (298 RMB tea), CASANOVA Italian (148 RMB sets).

Transportation: Metro Lines 2 and 10 to East Nanjing Road Station (10-15 minute walk). Bus Routes 37, 55, 147, 307.

sources.title: Shanghai Bund Guide: Top Spots, Tips & Things to Do
sources.content:
Step into Shanghai's past with a walk along the Bund, a 1.5-kilometer stretch of history, culture, and stunning architecture.

In 1844, the Bund became part of the British concession, marking the start of Shanghai's transformation. It features 52 stunning buildings in classical revival style, known as the Exhibition of World Architecture.

Best Things to Do: Stroll along the waterfront, take a night cruise, admire high-rises across the river, relax at Huangpu Park, watch locals exercise in early morning hours, catch sunset from Waibaidu Bridge.

Best Times: Spring and Fall (March-May, September-November). The lights come on around 6 p.m.

5-Kilometer Walking Route: Nanjing Road → Shanghai Postal Museum → Zhapu Road Bridge → Shama House → Fengyi Bund Origin → International Architecture Exhibition → The Bund → Lujiazui Trio → Pudong Art Museum.

Top Photo Spots: POP Roof Bar, The Bund Viewing Platform, Shama House, Shanghai Postal Museum, Waibaidu Bridge, People's Monument.

Budget Dining: Weixiang Zhai (sesame paste noodles), Dahuchun (fluffy pork buns), Lao Zhenghe (Michelin-starred eel), Xiande Lai (spareribs and rice cakes from novel Blossoms), Deda Western Restaurant (nearly 130 years).

sources.title: The Bund, Shanghai - What to See, Expert Tips, Map
sources.content:
The Bund contains 52 buildings of various architectural styles including Gothic, baroque, and neoclassical designs. It functions as a living museum of the colonial history of the 1800s.

Notable Buildings: Broadway Mansions, Astor House Hotel (contains museum), Peace Hotel (movie poster gallery), Hong Kong & Shanghai Bank (beautiful mosaic ceiling), Meteorological Signal Tower.

Walking Tours: 2.5-hour itinerary covering 1.3 kilometers. Evening visits provide amazing night views.

Huangpu River Cruises offer a distinctive contrast between historical architecture and modern skyscrapers.

Early morning visits reveal locals practicing tai chi and jogging. Best Viewpoints: Pudong Binjiang Avenue, Huangpu River cruises, Pudong skyscrapers.

Visit before sunset to enjoy golden light and evening illumination. Prepare umbrellas for rainy seasons, sun protection for sunny days.

sources.title: The Bund, Shanghai: Must-See Landmarks, Skyline Views & Tips
sources.content:
The Bund is a walking sightseeing zone on the west bank of the Huangpu river. Contains 33 buildings with varying architectural styles, termed the Exotic Building Clusters.

Notable structures: Peace Hotel, Waldorf Astoria Shanghai, Shanghai Pudong Development Bank (former HSBC Building), Bank of China Building.

Night Views: Illumination typically operates 19:00-23:00 nightly, extended during public holidays.

Free admission all day. Best visiting window: evening 19:00-20:00. Comfortable duration: 2-4 hours.

Sightseeing Tunnel: CNY 50 single trip, 646.7-meter transparent train journey beneath the Huangpu River.

Huangpu River Cruise: 45-minute journey from Shiliupu Pier. Avoid official Chinese holidays due to overcrowding.

sources.title: 外滩_百度百科
sources.content:
外滩（The Bund）位于上海市黄浦区黄浦江畔，是中国历史文化街区。全长1.5千米，南起延安东路，北至苏州河上的外白渡桥。

矗立52幢风格迥异的古典复兴大楼，被誉为外滩万国建筑博览群。1996年被列入全国重点文物保护单位。

名称由来：清末河流下游的黄浦江河滩被称为外黄浦滩，简称外滩。纤夫足迹踩出的曲折小道是外滩最早的路。

发展：1845年通过《上海土地章程》划为英租界。1854-1941年成为金融中心，有东方华尔街之称。1945年获正式路名中山东一路。

建筑风格：融汇英国古典式、法国大住宅式、哥特式、巴洛克式等多种风格。

主要景点：黄浦公园（1868年建立）、外白渡桥、十六铺码头、陈毅广场、外滩源、外滩观光隧道。全年全天开放，免费进入。

sources.title: Top 10 Things to see and do In the Bund, Shanghai
sources.content:
The Bund stretches 1.5 kilometers along the Huangpu River in Shanghai's Huangpu District. Since 1844 during the Qing Dynasty, this area was designated as part of the British Concession.

52 classical revival buildings line the Bund, also known as the World Architecture Exhibition. The landscape lighting is illuminated from 7:00-11:00 p.m. in summer and 6:00-10:00 p.m. in winter.

The promenade is open 24/7 and free of charge. Most stunning views after sunset when the lights come on.

Ferry Across the Huangpu: Cross to Lujiazui via a regular city ferry for 2 yuan. One of the most authentic and affordable ways to enjoy the views.

The Bund is crowded in the evening, especially during public holidays. Strong winds at night, bring a jacket. Multiple public restrooms along The Bund.
